items.d: **Line** performs the primary purpose (a district administration, a police station); **staff** advises and plans without command authority (the Cabinet Secretariat, planning cells); **auxiliary** provides common housekeeping services (DGS&D/GeM, the CPWD, Printing). Confusion between line and staff authority is the classic source of organisational conflict.

**Political versus permanent**; **single versus plural**; **real versus nominal**; and the **directly elected, indirectly elected, appointed** variants. In India the political executive is real and the permanent executive advises — the constitutional position from *Shamsher Singh* (1974).

**Delegation** — an authority transferring specified powers while retaining responsibility (revocable); **deconcentration** — dispersal of field offices without transfer of authority; **decentralisation** — a genuine transfer to lower levels; **devolution** — statutory transfer of functions, funds and functionaries to an autonomous elected body, as in the 73rd/74th Amendments. Precision here is a mark by itself.

**Legislative** (questions, committees, PAC/Estimates/COPU, cut motions), **executive** (hierarchy, inspection, vigilance, performance appraisal), **judicial** (writ, judicial review, tribunals), **quasi-judicial and ombudsman** (Lokpal, CVC, CIC, NHRC), and **citizen/social** (RTI, social audit, citizens' charters, report cards). The **CAG plus PAC** pairing is the strongest single accountability chain in India.

**Delegated legislation** — necessary but requiring safeguards; **Delhi Laws Act (1951)** held that essential legislative functions cannot be delegated. **Natural justice** — *nemo judex in causa sua* and *audi alteram partem*, extended to administrative action in **A.K. Kraipak (1969)** which blurred the quasi-judicial/administrative distinction; **reasoned orders**; and **Committee on Subordinate Legislation** in both Houses as the parliamentary check.

**Preventive versus punitive vigilance**; **collusive versus coercive corruption**; **state capture**; **integrity pact**; **red flags in procurement**; and the Second ARC's diagnosis that corruption thrives where there is **monopoly plus discretion minus accountability** (Klitgaard's equation: **C = M + D − A**) — the cleanest formula to write in an integrity answer.

**Citizens' Charter** (UK, 1991; India from 1997) with its six principles — quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency; **Sevottam** (service delivery excellence model, with three modules: charter implementation, grievance redress and service delivery capability); **RTI**; **social audit**; **e-governance**; and **Public Service Guarantee Acts** with penalties, which are what give a charter teeth.

**Position classification** (US) — the job is analysed and graded, and the person is recruited to the position; **career/rank classification** (UK, India) — the person is recruited to a service and moves through posts. India's system produces **generalist mobility and continuity but weak specialisation** — the standing argument for domain expertise and lateral entry.

The **Fulton Committee (1968, UK)** attacked the 'cult of the generalist' and recommended a unified grading structure and a Civil Service College. In India the **First ARC**, **Second ARC (10th Report)**, **Hota Committee (2004)**, **Baswan Committee (2016)** and **Mission Karmayogi** all push toward domain competence — while the counter-argument is that policy coordination itself is a specialised generalist skill.

India moved from the **Annual Confidential Report to the Performance Appraisal Report (2007-09)** — disclosure of the full report to the officer, the right to represent, numerical grading, and a **360-degree assessment for empanelment**. The critique: inflation of ratings, weak differentiation and no consequence for the middling performer.

**Line-item** (control), **performance** (management, output), **programme (PPBS)** (planning, outcome), **zero-base budgeting** (Peter Pyhrr; every rupee justified afresh; tried in India from 1987 with limited effect), **outcome budgeting** (India since 2005-06, now the Outcome Budget accompanying demands for grants), and **gender and child budgeting** (Gender Budget Statement since 2005-06).

**Preparation** (Ministry of Finance circular, estimates, pre-budget meetings) → **enactment** (presentation on **1 February**, general discussion, DRSC scrutiny of demands, guillotine, Appropriation Bill under Art. 114, Finance Bill under Art. 117 with the **75-day limit**) → **execution** (PFMS, re-appropriation, supplementary demands) → **audit** (CAG under Art. 149-151, then **PAC**). The **railway budget was merged in 2017** and the **plan/non-plan distinction abolished** the same year.

**Vote on Account** (advance for part of the year), **Supplementary, Additional, Excess (regularised after PAC scrutiny), Exceptional, Token grant** (to raise a discussion on a new service), and **Vote of Credit** ('blank cheque' for an unexpected demand). **Charged expenditure** (President's emoluments, salaries of the Speaker, judges, CAG, debt charges) is **non-votable** but discussable.

**Regularity/compliance audit** (was the expenditure authorised and within the rules), **propriety audit** (was it wise, faithful and economical — the discretionary and most contested form), and **performance/efficiency audit** (the '3 Es' — **economy, efficiency and effectiveness**), which is how the CAG examined 2G, coal and Ayushman Bharat.

**UK** — generalist tradition, Northcote-Trevelyan Report (1854) establishing **open competitive examination and merit**, permanent secretary, and the Next Steps agencies. **USA** — **Pendleton Act (1883)** ending the spoils system after Garfield's assassination, Office of Personnel Management, Senior Executive Service, and a large political appointee layer. **France** — ENA (replaced by INSP in 2022) and the grands corps. **China** — the cadre system under party supervision. India's is the **UK model plus constitutional protection (Art. 311) plus federal all-India services**.

**Fred Riggs, Edward Weidner** — administration for planned socio-economic change: **change-oriented, goal-oriented, innovative, client-oriented and temporally committed**. Its key claim is the **'administration of development' versus the 'development of administration'** distinction — you cannot deliver change with an unreformed machine.

**Buchanan, Tullock, Niskanen** — bureaucrats maximise **budget, staff and discretion**, not the public interest; hence the prescriptions of competition, contracting out and voucher systems. **Ostrom's** *The Intellectual Crisis in American Public Administration* proposed **polycentricity** against the single-centre bureaucratic paradigm. The intellectual foundation of NPM.

**G2C, G2B, G2G and G2E**; maturity stages — **closed/broadcasting/e-consultation/networked** (UNESCO), or **presence → interaction → transaction → transformation**. India's **National e-Governance Plan (2006) → Digital India (2015)**, with **DPI** as the new export doctrine; and the **Common Service Centres** as the assisted-access layer for those on the wrong side of the divide.

**Crisis management stages** — mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery; the **incident command system** adopted by NDMA; **Charles Perrow's normal accidents** (tightly coupled complex systems fail inevitably) against **high-reliability organisation theory** (they can be made not to). Use the pair whenever the question is why a well-designed system still failed.

**Work study and O&M**, **PERT and CPM** for project scheduling, **management by objectives (Drucker)**, **TQM and Kaizen**, **business process re-engineering**, **balanced scorecard**, **outcome frameworks (RFD — Results Framework Document, used in India from 2009-10)**, **decision support systems and data analytics**, and **behavioural nudges**. Naming the technique and its Indian application together is what earns the mark.
